title: BOS-572 (BOS-570 epic) — the Home session list fits a 72-column terminal by dropping its most expendable column instead of running off the right edge

scenes.title: the session board is fitted to a 72-column pty: NAME and STATUS survive, the board no longer overhangs the terminal

waitFor.label: the Home session table is drawn on the 72-column pty this scenario asked for

steps.caption: Home on a 72-column terminal: the demo board declares 73 columns of content, which no longer fits, so fitColumns drops the most expendable column
The fitted board sits inside the terminal — before BOS-572 these same columns were emitted at their full content width and clipped at the right edge

expect.label: NAME — priority 0, the row's identity, so it is never dropped no matter how narrow the terminal gets

STATUS — the most-scanned column, dropped last of the droppables, and still on screen at 72 columns because the demo board only overflows by a few columns (a longer-titled board drops it too, which is why the criterion this still cannot show — that REPO or PR is ABSENT — is carried by home_test.go instead)

steps.caption: The two columns the drop order protects are both present: NAME is priority 0 and STATUS is the last droppable to go
Arrow-navigating the fitted board: the cursor column is priority 0 too, so the chevron still tracks the selected row

expect.label: [n]ew session — the Home action bar is intact beneath the fitted table
[q]uit — the tail of the Home action bar is not clipped at the 72-column edge

steps.caption: The whole Home layout renders normally around the narrowed table: only the column set changed, not the screen
